unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'I recommend ordering these two parts; if only one fails, replacing both ensures the fault is fully resolved.'

rationale: The assistant sensibly refused to name a part at first and got the filter and vent hose cleared, but its opening check ignored that the customer said 'vented' by asking about a condenser unit, and it never asked about high vs low heat or the full model/serial. It leaned toward 'the heater element has failed open' when a one-shot thermal cut-out after a clogged hose is at least as likely, and once the customer said they had no multimeter it recommended buying both the element and cut-out rather than referring to an engineer, which the ground truth marks as the appropriate route. No invented evidence, no unsafe instruction (unplugging was stressed for the test), and no looping, but the ending is an unjustified shotgun parts purchase with no escalation.
